title: "Measures of Central Tendency for the Weibull Distribution"
author: "Anthony Morciglio"
date: "11/11/2025"
output: html_document

---

### 🧠 **Exploring Central Tendencies of the Weibull Distribution**

- **Weibull Parameters:** The shape and scale parameters define the distribution’s skewness and spread.
- **Measures of Central Tendency:**  
  - **Mean** and **Variance** use Gamma function relations.  
  - **Median** is derived from the inverse CDF (at 0.5).  
  - **Mode** exists only for shape > 1.
- **Visualization:**  
  - The shaded regions show **±1, ±2, ±3 standard deviations** from the mean.  
  - Vertical lines mark the **mean (blue)**, **median (green)**, and **mode (purple)**.  
  - The AUC shading helps visualize the probability concentration around the mean.

---


```{r, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ----------------------------------------------------------
# Description:
# This R code illustrates the measures of central tendency
# (mean, median, and mode) for a Weibull distribution and
# shows the area under the curve (AUC) for regions around
# the mean within a few standard deviations.
#
# It uses ggplot2 for visualization, and demonstrates:
# - How to compute the mean, median, and mode.
# - How to shade ±1, ±2, and ±3 standard deviation intervals.
# - How the Weibull distribution shape changes with parameters.
# ----------------------------------------------------------

# Load required packages
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Define Weibull parameters (shape and scale)
shape <- 2
scale <- 5

# Compute measures of central tendency
mean_wb <- scale * gamma(1 + 1/shape)
median_wb <- scale * (log(2))^(1/shape)
mode_wb <- if (shape > 1) scale * ((shape - 1)/shape)^(1/shape) else NA

# Compute variance and standard deviation
var_wb <- scale^2 * (gamma(1 + 2/shape) - (gamma(1 + 1/shape))^2)
sd_wb <- sqrt(var_wb)

# Create sequence for x values
x <- seq(0, 20, length.out = 1000)
pdf_vals <- dweibull(x, shape = shape, scale = scale)

# Create data frame for ggplot
df <- data.frame(x = x, pdf = pdf_vals)

# Define regions around the mean (±1, ±2, ±3 std)
region_data <- df %>%
  mutate(region = case_when(
    x >= mean_wb - sd_wb & x <= mean_wb + sd_wb ~ "±1 SD",
    x >= mean_wb - 2*sd_wb & x <= mean_wb + 2*sd_wb ~ "±2 SD",
    x >= mean_wb - 3*sd_wb & x <= mean_wb + 3*sd_wb ~ "±3 SD",
    TRUE ~ "Outside"
  ))

# Plot PDF with shaded AUC regions and central tendency markers
ggplot(region_data, aes(x, pdf)) +
  geom_area(data = subset(region_data, region == "±3 SD"), aes(fill = region), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_area(data = subset(region_data, region == "±2 SD"), aes(fill = region), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_area(data = subset(region_data, region == "±1 SD"), aes(fill = region), alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", size = 1.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean_wb, color = "blue", linetype = "solid", size = 1.1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = median_wb, color = "darkgreen", linetype = "dashed", size = 1.1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mode_wb, color = "purple", linetype = "dotted", size = 1.1) +
  annotate("text", x = mean_wb, y = max(df$pdf)*0.9, label = "Mean", color = "blue", hjust = -0.2) +
  annotate("text", x = median_wb, y = max(df$pdf)*0.8, label = "Median", color = "darkgreen", hjust = -0.2) +
  annotate("text", x = mode_wb, y = max(df$pdf)*0.7, label = "Mode", color = "purple", hjust = -0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("±1 SD" = "lightblue", "±2 SD" = "skyblue", "±3 SD" = "lightsteelblue")) +
  labs(
    title = "Weibull Distribution with Measures of Central Tendency",
    subtitle = paste0("Shape = ", shape, ", Scale = ", scale),
    x = "x",
    y = "Probability Density",
    fill = "Region"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

# Print summary of results
cat("Summary of Weibull Distribution Measures:\n")
cat(paste("Mean   =", round(mean_wb, 3), "\n"))
cat(paste("Median =", round(median_wb, 3), "\n"))
cat(paste("Mode   =", round(mode_wb, 3), "\n"))
cat(paste("SD     =", round(sd_wb, 3), "\n"))
```
